advisory.finding: A local release whose name is not an existing Jira version causes a hard per-mutation failure on every pass, forever. Each pass re-emits the outbound add (the name is in the intent set), the add fails, and the silent-no-op canary records an error, which makes the pass exit non-zero. That same outbound add also suppresses any inbound remove, so nothing ever resolves the mismatch.
scenarios: A user runs `rebar` to add release '2.5' before anyone creates version 2.5 in the Jira project: every reconcile pass from then on exits non-zero with silent-noop: releases
A misspelled release name blocks the pass from ever exiting clean, until someone either creates the version in Jira or edits the release in rebar

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Exclude inbound-origin names from SNAPSHOT-derived release intent (for example, have compaction preserve a non-inbound intent set) or narrow the documented guarantee, and add a post-compaction regression test

advisory.finding: The release intent set includes `SNAPSHOT.compiled_state.releases`. A compacted snapshot holds the full current release list, including names that only ever arrived inbound from Jira. After compaction those names count as local intent, so if someone later removes one of them in Jira, the outbound diff re-adds it, and that outbound add suppresses the inbound remove. This contradicts the new module's stated guarantee and the user docs.
scenarios: Jira adds version 3.0, which arrives inbound; the ticket is compacted into a SNAPSHOT; a Jira user removes 3.0; the next pass pushes add_fix_version(3.0) and the Jira-side removal is undone

No erratum or annotation exists in docs/adr/0124-jira-fix-versions-release-field.md (search for 'rratum' returned no matches)
advisory.finding: The outbound release diff limits ADDs to the ever-seen release intent set, and its module docstring credits this rule to ADR 0124 decisions 5 and 6. Accepted ADR 0124 decision 5 says the reconciler adds each local name the issue lacks and applies the intent-set limit only to removals. The change ships behavior that differs from the ADR without recording the change in the ADR, so the ADR's outbound decision is now inaccurate and the code comment cites it incorrectly.
scenarios: A contributor reads ADR 0124 decision 5, expects an inbound-only release name that Jira removed to be re-added by outbound sync, and treats the current behavior as a bug.
A reviewer checks the outbound_releases.py docstring against the ADR it cites and finds the ADR says the opposite about limiting ADDs.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add an annotation or erratum to docs/adr/0124-jira-fix-versions-release-field.md, next to decision 5, that keeps the original text. It should state that outbound ADDs are also limited to the ever-seen release intent set, so a Jira-side removal of an inbound-origin release is not undone. Alternatively, record a superseding ADR. Then make sure the outbound_releases.py docstring cites the annotated or superseding decision.

src/rebar/reconciler/outbound_releases.py: `for name in sorted(jira_names - local_names) if _intended(name)` — a remove needs the name to be absent locally, which never happens here because the inbound import adds it
The reconcile_once return value is never asserted and nothing checks that REB-1 got bound or imported, so 'no remove call' would also hold if the passes did nothing
Mitigation: the unit tests test_jira_release_rebar_never_held_is_never_removed and test_release_intent_gate_never_removes_a_name_rebar_never_held do cover the gate on the pure function
advisory.finding: The integration test `test_jira_version_rebar_never_held_is_never_removed` can't detect a regression in the remove gate it is named for. After the import pass, 'jira-only' is in the local ticket's releases (it arrives inbound), so local and Jira already agree and `_diff_releases` emits no remove whether or not the intent gate exists. The absence check on `write_calls` also has no check that the passes actually did anything.
scenarios: Someone deletes the `if _intended(name)` filter on removes: this integration test stays green
advisory.suggested_fix: First assert the binding exists (e.g. `_bindings(git_repo)` contains REB-1) and that `_releases(git_repo) == ["jira-only"]`. Then add a scenario where the ticket's local list really lacks a Jira name that is outside the intent set, and assert no `remove_fix_version` write.

Behaviour also changes once a SNAPSHOT compacts the ticket: `SNAPSHOT.compiled_state.releases` then puts inbound-origin names into the intent set, and no test covers the gate before vs. after compaction
advisory.finding: No test covers a local user removal of a release that first arrived inbound from Jira. With the new intent rules (inbound RELEASE_DELTA.added is excluded and `removed` is never folded in), that name is not in the intent set. So the outbound diff skips the remove, Jira keeps the version, and nothing pins what the next pass does.
scenarios: A user removes a Jira-sourced release in rebar: the removal is never pushed, and the next inbound pass may silently put it back locally, with no test documenting either outcome
After compaction the same removal starts being pushed, an untested behaviour flip

advisory.finding: The batch-path dispatcher's filter for malformed release entries is new and untested: an entry that isn't a dict, has an empty `release`, or has an action other than add/remove, and a `releases` value that isn't a list. Each of these is silently skipped and left out of `computed`.
scenarios: A refactor that counts malformed entries as computed would trip a false silent_noop, and the reverse change would let real drops go unreported; nothing would catch either
